q24141.en: On motorways and extra-urban roads, it is compulsory to switch on the dipped headlights also by day or, as an alternative, the daytime running lights.

explain.short: Outside towns cars must be easy to see also by day. So dipped beam, or daytime running lights instead, is compulsory.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'anche di giorno' (also by day) is correct here: the rule is not only for the night.

sceneParams.caption: Outside towns: dipped beam or daytime lights, also by day
lines: Dipped beam on, also by day

q24142.en: Wrong adjustment of the headlamp aim can reduce the driver's visibility or dazzle other road users.

explain.short: Headlamps aimed too low light too little road; aimed too high they shine into other drivers' eyes.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'può' (can) is fine: wrong aim does not always cause harm, but it can.

sceneParams.caption: Badly aimed headlamps: you see less or you dazzle
lines: Headlamps aimed too low: you see less
Aimed too high: you dazzle others

q24143.en: Badly aimed dipped headlights can dazzle other road users.

explain.short: If dipped headlights point too high, the light goes into the eyes of oncoming drivers, even if they are only dipped beam.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'male orientati' (badly aimed) is the key: even dipped beam dazzles if aimed wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam aimed too high still dazzles

q24144.en: Even with the dipped lights on, you risk dazzling others if the lamps are fitted wrongly or are not type-approved.

explain.short: Dipped beam is made not to dazzle, but only if the lamps are approved and fitted correctly.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'Pur avendo acceso le luci anabbaglianti' (even with dipped beam on): dipped beam does not protect you if the lamps are wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong or non-approved lamps can dazzle
lines: Lamps fitted wrong or not approved

q24145.en: On a motor vehicle it is not allowed to use lamps that are not type-approved.

explain.short: Lamps must be type-approved (omologate, officially tested) so their light is correct and does not dazzle.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'non è consentito' (not allowed) is correct: non-approved lamps are forbidden.

sceneParams.caption: Only type-approved lamps are allowed

q24146.en: Driving on an extra-urban road on a sunny day, it is enough to switch on the position lights.

explain.short: Outside towns you need dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Position lights alone are too weak.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'è sufficiente' (it is enough) is false: position lights are not enough, even in sunshine.

sceneParams.caption: Outside towns: dipped beam, not just position lights

q24147.en: Driving on an extra-urban road, it is compulsory to keep the main beam on during daytime hours.

explain.short: By day outside towns the dipped beam is compulsory, not the main beam. Main beam is never compulsory.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'abbaglianti' (main beam) instead of 'anabbaglianti' (dipped beam): one syllable changes everything.

sceneParams.caption: By day outside towns: dipped beam, not main beam

q24148.en: Using the position lights is compulsory at night when parked off the carriageway.

explain.short: A vehicle parked off the carriageway (the part of the road for traffic) is not in the way, so position lights are not compulsory.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'fuori della carreggiata' (off the carriageway): there lights are not required.

sceneParams.caption: Parked off the carriageway: no lights required

q24149.en: For the position lights you can use lamps of any colour.

explain.short: Position lights have fixed colours: white at the front, red at the back. Other colours are not allowed.
explain.rule: Outside towns use dipped beam (or daytime running lights) also by day. Headlamps must be well aimed and lamps approved (omologate), or you dazzle others.
explain.trap: 'qualsiasi colore' (any colour) is false: colours are fixed by law.

sceneParams.caption: Position lights: white in front, red behind

q24150.en: When driving in built-up areas, it is compulsory to keep the dipped lights on from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise.

explain.short: In towns, at night, you must drive with the dipped beam on. Night for lights starts half an hour after sunset and ends half an hour before sunrise.
explain.rule: At night and in poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam. Main beam is never compulsory. Parked: parking lights only on the carriageway, none off it or in a car park.
explain.trap: 'nei centri abitati' (in towns): street lights do not change this rule.

sceneParams.caption: In towns at night: dipped beam on
lines: From ½ h after sunset to ½ h before sunrise

q24151.en: While driving, when visibility is poor because of the weather (snow, rain, fog), it is compulsory to keep the position lights and the dipped lights on.

explain.short: In snow, rain or fog other drivers see you badly. Position lights and dipped beam make you visible.
explain.rule: At night and in poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam. Main beam is never compulsory. Parked: parking lights only on the carriageway, none off it or in a car park.
explain.trap: 'obbligatorio' (compulsory) is correct: lights are a must, not a choice.

sceneParams.caption: Poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam

q24152.en: While driving, in fog with visibility under 50 metres, you must use the rear fog light, if the vehicle has one.

explain.short: In thick fog the cars behind see you late. The bright red rear fog light helps them, but only when visibility is under 50 m.
explain.rule: At night and in poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam. Main beam is never compulsory. Parked: parking lights only on the carriageway, none off it or in a car park.
explain.trap: 'inferiore a 50 metri' (under 50 metres) is the official limit for the rear fog light.

sceneParams.caption: Fog under 50 m: rear fog light on
lines: Only if the car has one

q24153.en: At night, in built-up areas, a vehicle parked at the edge of the carriageway can be signalled with the parking lights.

explain.short: A car parked at the road edge at night must be visible. In towns the law allows the parking lights (luci di sosta) for this.
explain.rule: At night and in poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam. Main beam is never compulsory. Parked: parking lights only on the carriageway, none off it or in a car park.
explain.trap: 'può' (can) is correct: in towns parking lights are an allowed way to signal the parked car.

sceneParams.caption: Parked at night in town: parking lights allowed
lines: Parked at the edge of the road

q24154.en: While driving, it is compulsory to keep the main beam on from sunset to sunrise.

explain.short: Main beam (abbaglianti) is never compulsory: it is only allowed outside towns when it does not dazzle anyone. At night the dipped beam is compulsory.
explain.rule: At night and in poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam. Main beam is never compulsory. Parked: parking lights only on the carriageway, none off it or in a car park.
explain.trap: 'abbaglianti' (main beam) + 'obbligatorio': main beam is allowed, never compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: At night: dipped beam compulsory, main beam never

q24155.en: At night, when parked off the carriageway, it is compulsory to keep the dipped lights on.

explain.short: Off the carriageway the vehicle is not in the traffic, so no lights are needed. Dipped beam is a light for driving, not for parking.
explain.rule: At night and in poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam. Main beam is never compulsory. Parked: parking lights only on the carriageway, none off it or in a car park.
explain.trap: 'anabbaglianti' in 'sosta fuori dalla carreggiata': wrong light and no light needed there.

sceneParams.caption: Parked off the carriageway: no lights needed

q24156.en: If you leave the vehicle in an authorised car park, it is compulsory to keep the parking lights on the whole time.

explain.short: An authorised car park is not part of the traffic lane, so no lights are needed. Keeping them on would only drain the battery.
explain.rule: At night and in poor visibility: position lights + dipped beam. Main beam is never compulsory. Parked: parking lights only on the carriageway, none off it or in a car park.
explain.trap: 'parcheggio autorizzato' + 'per tutto il tempo': in a car park no lights are required.

sceneParams.caption: Authorised car park: no parking lights needed
lines: Car in an authorised car park

q24157.en: It is compulsory to switch on the dipped headlights, also by day, when driving through a tunnel.

explain.short: In a tunnel your eyes need time to adapt and others must see you. Dipped beam is compulsory in every tunnel.
explain.rule: Tunnel = dipped beam always, by day and even when it is well lit. Bad weather with poor visibility = lights on.
explain.trap: 'anche di giorno' (also by day) is correct: daylight outside does not matter.

sceneParams.caption: Tunnel: dipped beam on, also by day
lines: Dipped beam on, also by day

q24158.en: It is compulsory to switch on the vehicle's lights when visibility is poor because of the weather (fog, snow, rain).

explain.short: When fog, snow or rain hide you, the lights let other drivers see you in time.
explain.rule: Tunnel = dipped beam always, by day and even when it is well lit. Bad weather with poor visibility = lights on.
explain.trap: 'obbligatorio' (compulsory) is correct: not just a good idea.

sceneParams.caption: Bad weather, poor visibility: lights on

q24159.en: It is compulsory to switch on the dipped headlights in road tunnels only if they are poorly lit.

explain.short: Dipped beam is compulsory in every tunnel, also in well-lit ones. There is no exception for good lighting.
explain.rule: Tunnel = dipped beam always, by day and even when it is well lit. Bad weather with poor visibility = lights on.
explain.trap: 'solo se scarsamente illuminate' (only if poorly lit) is false: it applies to all tunnels.

sceneParams.caption: Every tunnel: dipped beam, even if well lit

q24160.en: While driving, in heavy rain, besides the dipped lights you must keep the rear fog light on, if the vehicle has one.

explain.short: Heavy rain makes you hard to see from behind, like fog. So the official rule adds the rear fog light to the dipped beam.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'pioggia intensa' (heavy rain) counts like fog for the rear fog light; light rain does not.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy rain: dipped beam + rear fog light
lines: Plus rear fog light, if fitted

q24161.en: While driving, in a heavy snowfall, besides the dipped lights you must keep the rear fog light on, if the vehicle has one.

explain.short: Thick snow hides you from the cars behind, like fog. So you add the rear fog light to the dipped beam.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'fitta nevicata' (heavy snowfall) counts like fog for the rear fog light.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy snow: dipped beam + rear fog light
lines: Plus rear fog light, if fitted

q24162.en: When driving outside built-up areas, it is compulsory to use the dipped lights, both by day and by night.

explain.short: Outside towns speeds are higher, so you must be seen from far. Dipped beam is compulsory day and night.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'sia di giorno che di notte' (both by day and by night) is correct outside towns.

sceneParams.caption: Outside towns: dipped beam day and night

keywords.it: sia di giorno che di notte
keywords.en: both by day and by night

q24163.en: Badly aimed dipped headlights can dazzle other road users.

explain.short: If dipped headlights point too high, the light goes into the eyes of oncoming drivers.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'male orientati' (badly aimed) is the key: even dipped beam dazzles if aimed wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam aimed too high still dazzles

q24164.en: When driving at night, using the dipped lights is compulsory even if the street lighting is enough.

explain.short: At night you need the dipped beam everywhere, also on well-lit streets, so that others see you.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'anche se l'illuminazione pubblica è sufficiente' (even if street lighting is enough): still compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: At night: dipped beam, even under street lights

q24165.en: While driving, using the dipped lights is not allowed in lit tunnels.

explain.short: Dipped beam is compulsory in every tunnel, also in lit ones. It is never forbidden there.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'non è consentito' (not allowed) is the opposite of the rule: it is compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: Lit tunnel: dipped beam compulsory, not forbidden

q24166.en: While driving, the position lights are always allowed as an alternative to the dipped lights.

explain.short: Position lights are too weak to drive with. When the dipped beam is compulsory, position lights cannot replace it.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) and 'in alternativa' (instead): position lights never replace dipped beam while driving.

sceneParams.caption: Position lights cannot replace dipped beam

q24167.en: Using the dipped lights is compulsory when you overtake a police car.

explain.short: There is no special light rule for overtaking a police car. You overtake it like any other vehicle.
explain.rule: Dipped beam: outside towns day and night, at night everywhere, in every tunnel. Heavy rain, thick snow or fog: add the rear fog light.
explain.trap: 'quando si sorpassa un'auto della polizia' (when overtaking a police car): an invented rule.

sceneParams.caption: Overtaking police: no special light rule

q24168.en: Reflectors are devices that reflect light.

explain.short: Reflectors (catadiottri) have no bulb: they send back the light of other vehicles' headlamps.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'riflettono' (reflect) is correct: they do not produce light.

sceneParams.caption: Reflectors send back light, they have no bulb

q24169.en: Reflectors fitted at the rear of vehicles are red.

explain.short: At the back of a vehicle lights and reflectors are red, so you know you are seeing its rear.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'colore rosso' (red) is right for the rear.

sceneParams.caption: Rear reflectors are red

q24170.en: Reflectors fitted at the rear of trailers and small trailers are red and triangular.

explain.short: Trailers have red triangular reflectors at the back, so you can tell a trailer from a car.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'triangolare' (triangular) is right for trailers only; on cars they are not triangular.

sceneParams.caption: Trailer rear reflectors: red triangles

q24171.en: Reflectors are also fitted on trailers and small trailers.

explain.short: Trailers also need to be seen at night, so they have reflectors too.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also) is correct: not only cars have reflectors.

sceneParams.caption: Trailers have reflectors too

q24172.en: Reflectors fitted at the front of trailers and small trailers are white.

explain.short: Front means white: white reflectors show the front of a trailer.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'parte davanti' (front) + 'bianco' (white) is the right pair.

sceneParams.caption: Trailer front reflectors are white

q24173.en: Reflectors must be switched on half an hour after sunset.

explain.short: Reflectors cannot be switched on: they have no bulb and only reflect light.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'vanno accesi' (must be switched on): reflectors are never switched on.

sceneParams.caption: Reflectors are never switched on

q24174.en: Reflectors must be switched on together with the position lights.

explain.short: Reflectors have no switch and no bulb. They work alone by reflecting light.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'vanno accesi' (must be switched on): reflectors are never switched on.

sceneParams.caption: Reflectors are never switched on

q24175.en: Reflectors replace the position lights when driving on urban roads.

explain.short: Reflectors only work when light hits them. They never replace the position lights, in towns or anywhere.
explain.rule: Reflectors reflect light, they are never switched on. Rear: red (triangular on trailers). Front of trailers: white.
explain.trap: 'sostituiscono' (replace) is false: reflectors are an extra, not a replacement.

sceneParams.caption: Reflectors never replace position lights

q24176.en: Reflectors show the presence and the size of the vehicles they are fitted on.

explain.short: Placed at the corners of a vehicle, reflectors show that it is there and how wide it is.
explain.rule: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and how big it is, mainly at night. They never signal turns or replace indicators.
explain.trap: 'ingombro' (size, space taken) is correct: they mark the vehicle's outline.

sceneParams.caption: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and its size
lines: You see the vehicle and its size

q24177.en: White reflectors are used to mark the front of trailers and semi-trailers.

explain.short: White means front: white reflectors show the front of trailers and semi-trailers.
explain.rule: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and how big it is, mainly at night. They never signal turns or replace indicators.
explain.trap: 'bianco' (white) = front, red = rear.

sceneParams.caption: White reflectors mark the front of trailers

q24178.en: Reflectors, when lit up, make vehicles and trailers parked on the road more visible, especially at night.

explain.short: When headlamps hit them, reflectors shine back, so a parked vehicle is seen in the dark.
explain.rule: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and how big it is, mainly at night. They never signal turns or replace indicators.
explain.trap: 'se illuminati' (when lit up by others' lights) is correct: they need outside light.

sceneParams.caption: Lit by headlamps, reflectors show parked vehicles

q24179.en: Reflectors make a broken-down vehicle more visible if the rear position lights do not work.

explain.short: Reflectors need no electricity, so they still work when the rear lights are broken.
explain.rule: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and how big it is, mainly at night. They never signal turns or replace indicators.
explain.trap: 'nel caso in cui non funzionino' (if they do not work) is correct: reflectors are a backup.

sceneParams.caption: Lights broken? Reflectors still show you

q24180.en: Reflectors, together with the direction indicators, signal that a vehicle is turning.

explain.short: Only the indicators signal a turn. Reflectors just show that the vehicle is there.
explain.rule: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and how big it is, mainly at night. They never signal turns or replace indicators.
explain.trap: 'segnalano la svolta' (signal the turn): reflectors never do that.

sceneParams.caption: Reflectors do not signal turns

q24181.en: White reflectors are fitted on motor vehicles carrying flammable material.

explain.short: White reflectors mark the front of trailers. They have nothing to do with dangerous loads.
explain.rule: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and how big it is, mainly at night. They never signal turns or replace indicators.
explain.trap: 'materiale infiammabile' (flammable material): an invented link.

sceneParams.caption: White reflectors = front of trailers, not loads

q24182.en: Reflectors can replace the direction indicators.

explain.short: Indicators flash to show a turn; reflectors cannot flash or signal anything. They are not a replacement.
explain.rule: Reflectors show where a vehicle is and how big it is, mainly at night. They never signal turns or replace indicators.
explain.trap: 'sostituire' (replace) is false: nothing replaces the indicators.

sceneParams.caption: Reflectors cannot replace indicators

q24183.en: The rear number plate of a motor vehicle is lit so its characters can be read easily.

explain.short: Police and cameras must read the plate also in the dark, so it has its own light.
explain.rule: The rear plate light is white, so the plate can be read. It works together with the position lights.
explain.trap: 'facile lettura' (easy reading) is exactly the reason for the plate light.

sceneParams.caption: Plate light: so the plate can be read
lines: Lit so it can be read

q24184.en: The rear number plate of a motor vehicle must be lit with a white light.

explain.short: The plate light is white, so the plate is read with its true colours.
explain.rule: The rear plate light is white, so the plate can be read. It works together with the position lights.
explain.trap: 'luce bianca' (white light) is correct; not red or other colours.

sceneParams.caption: Rear plate light: white

q24185.en: The number plate light of a motor vehicle must be switched on only at night.

explain.short: The plate light comes on with the position lights, so it is on also by day when lights are needed (outside towns, tunnels, bad weather).
explain.rule: The rear plate light is white, so the plate can be read. It works together with the position lights.
explain.trap: 'solo di notte' (only at night) is false: it works whenever the position lights are on.

sceneParams.caption: Plate light on with position lights, not only at night

q24186.en: The number plate light of a motor vehicle must stay on if you park off the road.

explain.short: Parked off the road you are out of traffic, so no lights are needed, plate light included.
explain.rule: The rear plate light is white, so the plate can be read. It works together with the position lights.
explain.trap: 'fuori dalla strada' (off the road): there no light must stay on.

sceneParams.caption: Parked off the road: plate light can be off

q24187.en: The tell-tale for the hazard warning lights is red.

explain.short: The hazard lights are used in danger, so their tell-tale (spia, dashboard light) is red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is correct: this tell-tale warns of danger or something important.

sceneParams.caption: Hazard lights tell-tale: red

q24188.en: The tell-tale for the coolant temperature is red.

explain.short: If the engine coolant gets too hot the engine can be damaged: the tell-tale is red. Stop and check.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is correct: this tell-tale warns of danger or something important.

sceneParams.caption: Coolant temperature tell-tale: red

q24189.en: The tell-tale for the oil pressure is red.

explain.short: Low oil pressure can quickly ruin the engine, so its tell-tale is red. Stop the engine.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is correct: this tell-tale warns of danger or something important.

sceneParams.caption: Oil pressure tell-tale: red

q24190.en: The tell-tale for the seat belt is red.

explain.short: An unfastened seat belt is a safety danger, so its tell-tale is red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is correct: this tell-tale warns of danger or something important.

sceneParams.caption: Seat belt tell-tale: red

q24191.en: The tell-tale for the handbrake is red.

explain.short: Driving with the handbrake on damages the brakes, so its tell-tale is red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is correct: this tell-tale warns of danger or something important.

sceneParams.caption: Handbrake tell-tale: red

q24192.en: The tell-tale for the direction indicators is red.

explain.short: The indicator tell-tale only shows that the indicator is flashing. It is green, not red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is false: this tell-tale only shows that a device is on, so it is green.

sceneParams.caption: Indicators tell-tale: green, not red

q24193.en: The tell-tale for the dipped lights is red.

explain.short: The dipped beam tell-tale just shows the lights are on. It is green, not red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is false: this tell-tale only shows that a device is on, so it is green.

sceneParams.caption: Dipped beam tell-tale: green, not red

q24194.en: The tell-tale for the main beam is red.

explain.short: The main beam tell-tale is blue, to remind you to switch to dipped beam when meeting others. It is not red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is false: this tell-tale only shows that a device is on, so it is blue.

sceneParams.caption: Main beam tell-tale: blue, not red

q24195.en: The tell-tale for the fog lights is red.

explain.short: Fog light tell-tales only show the lights are on: green for the front fog lights, yellow for the rear one. Never red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is false: this tell-tale only shows that a device is on, so it is green or yellow.

sceneParams.caption: Fog lights tell-tale: green or yellow, not red

q24196.en: The tell-tale for the windscreen defrosting or demisting device is red.

explain.short: The demister tell-tale only shows that the windscreen heater is on. It is yellow (amber), not red.
explain.rule: Red tell-tale = danger: hazard lights, coolant temperature, oil pressure, seat belt, handbrake. Green/blue/yellow = a device is on.
explain.trap: 'rosso' (red) is false: this tell-tale only shows that a device is on, so it is yellow.

sceneParams.caption: Demister tell-tale: yellow, not red
